newsitem.title: USA: Portuguese leader backs NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese leader backs NATO expansion.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres met with President Bill Clinton on Thursday and strongly supported NATO expansion, but said the alliance must preserve a "very special relationship" with Russia.
Clinton, in turn, praised Guterres for "progressive and strong leadership" and said thanked him for Portugal's involvement in peacekeeping operations in Bosnia and Africa.
Before the two leaders met, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said European security would top their agenda.
Guterres, fielding reporters' questions at the start of his talks with Clinton, said NATO expansion was "a basic condition for democracy, for peace and stability in central and eastern Europe."

NATO leaders are to meet in Madrid in July to decide which will be the first nations invited to join an enlarged alliance. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be among the first new members.

"Of course, we understand that it is very important to preserve the very special relationship with the new Russia," Guterres said. "I hope that one day in the future NATO and Russia can be allies, defending the values of enlightenment against all the irrational behaviours in the modern world."
